issues.legal_issue: Heirs of a partner in a sub-partnership may have a prima facie interest in immovable property where the partnership’s property rights were later crystallised and acknowledged in subsequent documents.
material_facts: The deceased had a fractional share in a sub-partnership whose partners’ interests were connected with a share in the main partnership.

Before the deceased died, the main partners agreed to divide the property, and a later registered partition deed allocated property to one group while recording that it would fulfil obligations to its sub-partners.

A later registered rectification deed, whose certified copy contained handwritten additions, prima facie recognised the sub-partners’ property interests; the court found the surrounding evidence supported that those additions were present before registration.
Later correspondence from partners acknowledged the sub-partners’ rights in the property.
A purported release deed by the deceased’s heirs referred to a suit filed after the date of the release deed.
issues.conclusion: For the interlocutory application, the heirs had made out a prima facie case that they retained an interest in the property, and the purported release deed prima facie appeared to be forged.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the documents and surrounding circumstances only to determine whether a prima facie case existed on an application under Order 39 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure; its observations were not to affect the trial on the merits.

predicates.later_registered_partition_allocated_pro: The main partners later executed a registered deed allocating property between their groups and referring to obligations to sub-partners.
predicates.later_registered_rectification_recognise: A registered rectification deed contained additions that identified sub-partners as having interests in the allocated property.
predicates.later_partner_correspondence_acknowledge: Partners later exchanged correspondence acknowledging the sub-partners’ rights in the property.
predicates.release_referred_to_later_filed_suit: A purported release deed by the heirs referred to a suit that was filed after the date shown on that deed.

issues.definition: When an interlocutory injunction appeal involves a deceased partner’s sub-partnership share, a later registered property allocation and rectification recognising sub-partners, later acknowledgments of their property rights, and a release deed referring to a later-filed suit, a prima facie inherited property interest is established.

issues.legal_issue: A limitation objection to dissolution and accounts does not by itself defeat distinct claims for declaration of property rights and related relief when subsequent documents prima facie evidence an interest in the property.
material_facts: The suit sought not only dissolution of the sub-partnership and accounts, but also declaration of title, partition, injunction, damages, and other reliefs.
The defendants argued that because the deceased had died long before the suit, claims for dissolution and accounts were time-barred and the heirs could claim no property relief.
The court identified subsequent registered and other documents that prima facie evidenced the heirs’ rights in the immovable property.
issues.conclusion: At the interlocutory stage, it was not permissible to treat a possible bar to dissolution or accounts as necessarily defeating the other claims concerning the property.
issues.legal_principle: In assessing an application under Order 39 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a claim for dissolution and accounts must be distinguished from separate claims for declaration of title and other property relief; the court did not finally determine limitation or the suit’s merits.

predicates.interlocutory_injunction_appeal: The matter arose in an appeal concerning temporary relief pending trial of a suit.
predicates.suit_claims_property_relief_beyond_accou: The suit sought property-related remedies in addition to dissolution and accounts.
predicates.limitation_objection_targets_dissolution: The opposing side argued that the claims for dissolution or accounts were time-barred.
predicates.later_documents_support_property_interes: Documents made after the relevant partner’s death prima facie evidenced an interest in the property.

issues.definition: When an interlocutory injunction appeal concerns a suit seeking property remedies beyond accounts, a limitation objection directed at dissolution or accounts, and later documents supporting a property interest, that objection does not automatically defeat the other relief.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser with actual or constructive notice of another person’s property interest cannot claim to be a purchaser without notice of that interest.
material_facts: A registered rectification deed prima facie recognised the sub-partners’ interest in the property.
The purchaser’s agreement with one group referred to the rectification deed, while the purchaser’s agreement with another group described the sub-partners’ rights as claims.
The purchaser thus had actual notice from the transaction documents and constructive notice of the registered rectification deed.
The purchaser also obtained an agreement from a sub-partner for transfer of existing rights in the property.
issues.conclusion: The purchaser could not, at the interlocutory stage, rely on a plea that it was a bona fide purchaser without notice of the sub-partners’ rights.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 3 of the Transfer of Property Act, a person has notice of a fact actually known to them or which they would have known but for wilful abstention from inquiry or gross negligence; Explanation I deems an acquirer to have notice of a registered instrument relating to immovable property. The court also applied the principle that a transferor cannot convey an interest that the transferor does not have.

predicates.interlocutory_injunction_appeal: The notice question arose in an appeal concerning temporary relief pending a suit.
predicates.purchaser_acquired_property_interest: A purchaser entered into agreements to acquire development or property interests.
predicates.registered_instrument_recorded_other_int: A registered instrument recorded another group’s interest in the property.
predicates.transaction_documents_disclosed_instrume: The purchaser’s transaction documents referred to the instrument or disclosed the other group’s claimed interest.

issues.definition: When a purchaser acquires a property interest in an interlocutory injunction case and a registered instrument records another interest that the transaction documents disclose, the purchaser cannot claim to have purchased without notice.

issues.legal_issue: General authority to manage a partnership’s affairs does not, without express authority, empower a partner to transfer immovable property belonging to the firm.
material_facts: The partnership deed stated that a named partner would manage the partnership’s affairs and that what he did would bind the partners.
The deed did not expressly authorise that partner to transfer the firm’s immovable property.
The builder relied on that clause to argue that the partner’s dealings with the property bound the other partners.
issues.conclusion: The management clause did not prima facie authorise the partner to transfer the partnership’s immovable property or bind the other partners to such a transfer.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 19(1) of the Partnership Act, acts done by a partner in the usual way of the firm’s business bind the firm. Section 19(2)(g) provides that, absent a contrary usage or custom, that authority does not include transferring immovable property belonging to the firm; such authority must be expressly given.

predicates.partner_received_general_management_auth: The partnership deed gave a partner general authority to manage the firm’s affairs and made his acts binding on the partners.
predicates.firm_property_was_immovable: The property the partner purported to deal with belonged to the firm and was immovable property.
predicates.deed_lacked_express_transfer_authority: The partnership deed contained no express authority for the partner to transfer the firm’s immovable property.

issues.definition: When a partner has general management authority over a firm that owns immovable property but the deed gives no express power to transfer it, that general authority does not authorise the transfer.

issues.legal_issue: A temporary injunction may be granted to protect a prima facie property interest from construction that could make the dispute’s outcome irreversible, despite delay or expenditure, where the balance of convenience favours protection and no adequate safeguard is offered.
material_facts: The heirs had made out a prima facie case of an interest in the property.
The builder proposed construction using the floor-space index of the property as a whole, including land in which the heirs claimed an interest.
The heirs had delayed bringing the suit, and the builder had publicised its plans and spent substantial sums on construction.
The court considered the delay in light of assurances to the sub-partners, the disputed release deed, and the denial of their rights.
The builder and the other opposing parties did not offer adequate terms to safeguard the heirs’ interests.
The court found that the proposed use of the floor-space index could prejudice the heirs and that protection was warranted pending trial.
issues.conclusion: The court set aside the lower courts’ orders and granted a temporary injunction restraining construction and dealings affecting the disputed property through use of the floor-space index for the whole land, while permitting an application to modify the order on adequate safeguards.
issues.legal_principle: Order 39 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits temporary injunctive relief where the applicant establishes grounds for protection pending suit. Applying the approach in Gangubai B. Chaudhary v. Sitaram B. Sukhtankar, [1983] 4 SCC 31, the court considered whether construction could make the dispute irreversible, the balance of convenience, the parties’ conduct, and whether adequate safeguards were offered.

rule.if: interlocutory_injunction_appeal and prima_facie_property_interest and proposed_construction_threatens_irreversible_prejudice and development_uses_floor_space_index_of_whole_land and no_adequate_safeguard_offered

issues.definition: When an interlocutory injunction appeal involves a prima facie property interest, proposed construction threatening irreversible prejudice, development using the whole land’s floor-space index, and no adequate safeguard, a temporary injunction is granted pending suit.
